content:
Currently, whitespace and comments at the start of lean blocks effectively are handled as follows:

  • In the manual genre leading whitespace is stripped, but comments before the first command are kept.
  • In the blog genre leading whitespace and comments are stripped.

So, in the manual genre

```lean


-- A comment preceded by two empty lines and followed by one

#eval 1
```

becomes rendered as

-- A comment preceded by two empty lines and followed by one

#eval 1

whereas in the blog genre (after adding some exampleContext), it gets rendered as:

#eval 1

(Note that this is not changed by verso#924.) Apart from that:

  • Both genres effectively do not permit just empty lines or comments in a lean block.

In my opinion, the content of lean blocks should just faithfully carry over to the generated output. I.e., neither leading whitespace nor leading comments should be stripped, and it should be possible to have lean blocks with just comments.

I would try to fix that myself (and learn more about Lean and Verso along the way). But first I wanted to gauge the opinion of the Verso maintainers on this.
